title: Colours, fonts and size
text: Choose palette name. options "default" (blue, red grey, used everywhere else guides), "okabe_ito", "viridis" "greyscale". "okabe_ito" uses blue vermillion Okabe–Ito palette, designed stay distinguishable people common types colour blindness:  "viridis":  "greyscale", black--white printing:

title: Colours, fonts and size
text: Give three colours: positive effects, negative effects, effects whose interval includes null value. colour name hex code works:
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", vi = "vi",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   palette = c(positive = "#1b7837", negative = "#762a83", null = "grey75") )

code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", vi = "vi",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   y_label = "Hedges' g (95% CI)",   x_label = "Studies, sorted by effect size" )

text: numbers along study axis study’s rank effect size. rarely matter readers, study_ticks = FALSE removes tick marks:
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", vi = "vi",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   study_ticks = FALSE )

title: Effect sizes and axes
text: Colours depend whether confidence interval excludes value meaning “effect”. ’s 0 differences (log ratios) 1 ratios odds ratios. Odds-ratio intervals aren’t symmetric, give bounds lb ub rather variance. example effects converted odds ratios:  Ratios often easier read log scale: plot log() variance (vi) default null_value = 0.
code: odds <- forestmap_example to_log_or <- pi / sqrt(3) odds$or <- exp(odds$smd * to_log_or) odds$or_lower <- exp((odds$smd - 1.96 * sqrt(odds$vi)) * to_log_or) odds$or_upper <- exp((odds$smd + 1.96 * sqrt(odds$vi)) * to_log_or)  plot_forestmap(   odds, "or", "or_lower", "or_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   null_value = 1,   y_label = "Odds ratio (95% CI)" )

what: Effects too small to matter: rope
title: Effect sizes and axes
text: rope shades band effects consider small matter (“region practical equivalence”). Give two numbers, one number band symmetric around null_value:
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", vi = "vi",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   rope = c(-0.1, 0.1) )

title: Effect sizes and axes
text: default y-axis symmetric around null_value wide enough show every confidence interval (ratios, starts 0). Set range y_limits; parts intervals outside cut :
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", vi = "vi",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   y_limits = c(-1, 1.2) )

title: Adding to the plot and saving
text: plot_forestmap() returns patchwork ggplot2 plots: p[[1]] forest plot p[[2]] heatmap. (continuous_range = "legend", p[[3]] holds legends.) can add either one.

title: Adding to the plot and saving
code: p <- plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", vi = "vi",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design") )  p + patchwork::plot_annotation(   title = "Effects of the intervention",   subtitle = "60 studies, sorted by effect size",   caption = "Simulated data" )

title: Adding to the plot and saving
text: Add line forest plot, example pooled effect meta-analysis. ’s simple inverse-variance (fixed-effect) average:  Text added annotate() doesn’t pick plot’s font automatically, set family font plot uses ("Roboto Condensed" unless chose another).
code: pooled <- weighted.mean(forestmap_example$smd, w = 1 / forestmap_example$vi)  p <- plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", vi = "vi",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design") )  p[[1]] <- p[[1]] +   ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = pooled, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +   ggplot2::annotate(     "text", x = 1, y = pooled, label = "Pooled effect",     hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3, family = "Roboto Condensed"   ) p

title: Adding to the plot and saving
text: Change y-axis labels go scale_y_continuous(). Use round numbers; seq() can create tiny rounding errors show odd labels:
code: p <- plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", vi = "vi",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design") )  p[[1]] <- p[[1]] + ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1)) p

title: Adding to the plot and saving
text: plot_forestmap() doesn’t save anything; use ggplot2::ggsave() choose size . plot looks best around 7 × 5 inches four properties; add height add rows. PDFs, use device = cairo_pdf. PDFs (RStudio’s Plots pane) see fonts installed computer, install Roboto Condensed (system.file("fonts", package = "forestmap")) choose installed font. RStudio can instead set Tools > Global Options > General > Graphics > Backend AGG.
code: ggplot2::ggsave("forestmap.png", p, width = 7, height = 5.25, dpi = 300) ggplot2::ggsave("forestmap.svg", p, width = 7, height = 5.25) ggplot2::ggsave("forestmap.pdf", p, width = 7, height = 5.25, device = cairo_pdf)

title: Getting started with forestmap
text: forest plot shows study meta-analysis effect size confidence interval. forestmap sorts studies smallest largest effect adds heatmap underneath showing study’s properties: population, design, country, anything else ’ve coded. Reading column tells one study; reading across row tells studies property fall among effects.

title: Getting started with forestmap
text: need data frame one row per study columns: package comes made-data 60 studies: order factor’s levels sets order rows heatmap, use factor(x, levels = ...) change . ’ve computed effect sizes metafor’s escalc(), data already effect (yi) sampling variance (vi): pass es = "yi", vi = "vi". Instead variances can give standard errors (se = "..."), lower upper bounds 95% confidence interval (lb = "...", ub = "..."). Use bounds interval isn’t symmetric, odds ratios original scale. variances standard errors, interval effect ± 1.96 standard errors.
code: head(forestmap_example) #>         study   smd      vi   n population     outcome             design #> 1   Wang 2005 0.470 0.01581 253   Children        <NA>                RCT #> 2 Hughes 2013 0.261 0.03704 108   Children Behavioural                RCT #> 3  Rossi 2005 0.510 0.04545  88     Adults Self-report Quasi-experimental #> 4  Baker 2006 0.410 0.01493 268     Adults        <NA> Quasi-experimental #> 5 Hughes 2008 0.786 0.03077 130   Children Self-report                RCT #> 6 Martin 2023 0.260 0.06349  63     Adults        <NA>                RCT #>     country #> 1       USA #> 2      <NA> #> 3    Canada #> 4 Australia #> 5       USA #> 6       USA

title: Large meta-analyses
text: forestmap_example data 60 studies. larger example, draw 250 effects random add little noise, two : Plot usual:  effect column, 0.4% plot’s width. 60 effects, points, interval lines white borders heatmap tiles get thinner, neighbouring effects don’t merge block. plot reads pattern rather single studies: colour bands show ranking studies property fall, sample-size row shows whether larger studies find smaller effects.
code: set.seed(1) big <- forestmap_example[sample(nrow(forestmap_example), 250, replace = TRUE), ] big$smd <- big$smd + rnorm(nrow(big), 0, 0.1) plot_forestmap(   big, "smd", vi = "vi",   moderators = c(     "Population" = "population",     "Study design" = "design",     "Sample size" = "n"   ) )

title: Large meta-analyses
text: rank numbers along study axis say little 250 effects, study_ticks = FALSE removes . compact layout, property names left rows, makes heatmap shorter leaves room forest plot. max_levels merges rare levels “”, property fewer, fuller rows:  Give plot plenty width save . rough guide, allow 0.04 inches per effect, least 8 inches:
code: plot_forestmap(   big, "smd", vi = "vi",   moderators = c(     "Population" = "population",     "Study design" = "design",     "Country" = "country",     "Sample size" = "n"   ),   layout = "compact",   max_levels = 4,   study_ticks = FALSE,   x_label = "250 effects, sorted by effect size" ) p <- plot_forestmap(big, "smd", vi = "vi", moderators = c("Population" = "population")) ggplot2::ggsave("forestmap.png", p, width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 300)

title: Forest plot of studies with a heatmap of study properties — plot_forestmap
text: data data frame one row per study. es Name column holding study's effect size. lb, ub Names columns holding lower upper bounds study's 95% confidence interval. Give , vi, se. moderators Names columns holding study properties (factors). Name vector set moderator's heading, e.g. c("Study design" = "design", "Population" = "population"); unnamed entries use column name. vi Name column holding study's sampling variance (e.g. vi metafor::escalc()). 95% confidence interval computed es ± 1.96 × √vi. Use instead lb ub. se Name column holding study's standard error. 95% confidence interval computed es ± 1.96 × se. Use instead lb ub. font font family installed computer (e.g. "Helvetica"), path .ttf/.otf font file. default, "Roboto Condensed", comes package, works every computer. palette palette name forestmap_palettes ("default", "okabe_ito", "viridis", "greyscale") three colours, e.g. c(positive = "darkgreen", negative = "purple", null = "grey"). text_size Base text size points. forest_height Share plot given forest plot, 0 1: share height, width orientation = "vertical" (0.5 gives forest plot heatmap equal space). "auto" (default) gives heatmap room rows (columns) . null_value value meaning "effect": 0 differences log ratios, 1 raw ratios odds ratios. rope Optional region practical equivalence, drawn shaded band: two numbers c(-0.1, 0.1), one number band symmetric around null_value. y_limits Optional limits effect size axis (y-axis, x-axis orientation = "vertical"), e.g. c(-1, 1). default axis symmetric around null_value shows every confidence interval full; ratios (null_value 0 every value positive) starts 0. y_label, x_label Axis titles: y_label effect sizes, x_label studies. vertical orientation study axis title unless give x_label. max_levels Optional maximum number rows per moderator. max_levels = 3, 2 common levels shown rest merged one "" row. levels tie last place, kept (warning). NULL (default) shows every level. layout "standard" puts bold heading moderator's rows; "compact" puts moderator name left rows instead, makes heatmap shorter. continuous_style continuous (numeric) moderators show study's value: "bar" (default), "tint" "stripe". See Moderators. continuous_range show range continuous moderator: "none" (default), "label" (row's label, e.g. "Mean age (19-67)"), "end" (small key end row, column vertical) "legend" (plot). orientation "horizontal" (default) puts forest plot heatmap, studies along x-axis. "vertical" puts one study per row, heatmap right. See Orientation. study Optional name column holding study names (e.g. "Smith 2019"), shown beside row orientation = "vertical". label_size Optional text sizes, points, plot's labels, named study (study names), level (moderator levels) moderator (moderator names), e.g. c(study = 6, level = 8). Labels name follow text_size (study names 85% ). Make labels smaller stop overlapping many studies levels. level_angle Angle, degrees 0 (flat) 90 (upright), level labels heatmap's columns orientation = "vertical". study_ticks Show tick marks numbers study axis (x-axis, y-axis orientation = "vertical")? numbers study's rank effect size. FALSE removes keeps axis line. Study names (study) shown either way.

title: Forest plot of studies with a heatmap of study properties — plot_forestmap
code: p <- plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example,   es = "smd", vi = "vi",   moderators = c(     "Population" = "population",     "Outcome measure" = "outcome",     "Study design" = "design",     "Country" = "country"   ),   rope = c(-0.1, 0.1),   y_label = "SMD (95% CI)" ) p   # With confidence interval bounds instead of variances dat <- forestmap_example dat$ci_lower <- dat$smd - 1.96 * sqrt(dat$vi) dat$ci_upper <- dat$smd + 1.96 * sqrt(dat$vi) plot_forestmap(   dat, es = "smd", lb = "ci_lower", ub = "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design") )   # A continuous moderator (sample size), shown as bars with a legend plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", vi = "vi",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Sample size" = "n"),   continuous_style = "bar",   continuous_range = "legend" )   # Vertical, with study names, for long meta-analyses plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", vi = "vi",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   orientation = "vertical",   study = "study",   label_size = c(study = 7) )   # Compact layout, Okabe-Ito palette plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", vi = "vi",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   palette = "okabe_ito",   layout = "compact" )   if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ggplot2::ggsave("forestmap.png", p, width = 7, height = 5.25, dpi = 300) } # }
